name: Johnny Long
org: Hackers for Charity (founder); formerly penetration tester and author with Syngress
why_notable: Security researcher who in 2002 began cataloguing Google search queries that exposed vulnerable systems and sensitive files, naming them googleDorks and turning a search box into a reconnaissance tool. The collection became the Google Hacking Database (GHDB) in 2004; he presented Google hacking at Black Hat 2004 and DEF CON 13 (2005) and wrote the field's foundational book, Google Hacking for Penetration Testers (Syngress, Dec 2004; Vol. 2 2007; 3rd ed. 2015 with Bill Gardner and Justin Brown), plus No Tech Hacking. In 2010, before leaving on a long-term volunteer mission to Uganda, he handed the GHDB to Offensive Security, which still curates it on Exploit-DB. He founded Hackers for Charity, which places technologists' skills in the service of non-profits. Every pentester, bug bounty hunter or OSINT analyst who opens an engagement with site:/filetype: queries is using the method he popularised.
